chordInfo.name: Suspended Chords
chordInfo.subtitle: Create tension and release with suspended chords - ambiguous, floating harmony that adds movement and interest to your playing.

fundamentals.label: Definition
fundamentals.value: Three-note chords where the 3rd is replaced by 2nd or 4th

boxes.title: Interval Quality
items: Tension: Wants to resolve to major or minor

boxes.title: Scale Relationship
items: Resolution: Sus4 resolves down to major 3rd
Resolution: Sus2 resolves up to major 3rd
Color: Adds movement without key change

voicingGroups.title: Essential Suspended Chord Voicings
voicingGroups.tipDescription: These are the fundamental suspended chord voicings for guitar.

voicings.name: Dsus4
voicings.use: Resolves to D major, rock riffs

items.title: Sus4 Resolution Pattern
items.description: Classic sus4-to-major resolution pattern - creates satisfying tension and release heard in rock anthems like "Pinball Wizard".

techniqueItems: Practice lifting fingers for sus4 to major resolution
Focus on smooth transitions between sus and resolved chords
Use hammer-ons and pull-offs for ornamental suspensions
Keep steady rhythm while resolving suspensions
applicationItems: Adds movement to static chord progressions
Essential for rock and folk embellishments
Perfect for intro riffs and arpeggiated patterns

practiceExercises.title: Practice Exercises
practiceExercises.tipDescription: These exercises will help you master suspended chords and their resolutions.

exercises.title: Exercise 1: Sus4 Resolution Practice
exercises.detail: Practice resolving sus4 chords to their major counterparts
exercises.tip: Focus on the single finger movement that creates the resolution

concepts.title: Creative Suspended Chord Uses
items: Sus as modal color: Neither major nor minor
Parallel sus movement: Moving shapes up neck
Pedal tone suspensions: Holding bass while moving

journeySection.title: Continue Your Chord Journey
journeySection.description: Now that you understand suspended chords, explore how they connect to other chord types and advanced harmonic concepts.

links.title: Major Chords
links.description: Return to the bright foundation that suspended chords resolve to.
